result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides, but the pedestrian environment is constrained by narrow walkways on the right and frequent vehicle access points on the left. Parked cars along the curb create visual obstructions, and the lack of traffic calming measures or a buffer zone reduces overall pedestrian comfort and safety.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Cars
hazards.description: A continuous line of parked vehicles on the right side of the street blocks sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers on the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street along the curb

hazards.name: Frequent Vehicle Conflict Points
hazards.description: The left side of the street has multiple curb cuts and a large open parking area, increasing the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflicts across the walkway.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the intersection and crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffers
interventions.description: Add a planting strip or street trees to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and moving traffic.

result.summary: The image shows a dense residential street with row houses and a very narrow sidewalk significantly obstructed by utility poles and building stoops. While a pedestrian crossing sign is present, there is no visible marked crossing or other protective infrastructure for pedestrians in the immediate vicinity.

hazards.name: Narrow and Obstructed Sidewalk
hazards.description: The utility pole and building stoops significantly reduce the effective width of the sidewalk, forcing pedestrians into a very narrow path.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image, along the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossing
hazards.description: A pedestrian crossing sign is present, but there is no corresponding marked crosswalk visible, which may lead to confusion for both drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Roadway area near the yellow sign.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Increase the width of the sidewalk to meet accessibility standards and provide a clear path of travel around obstructions like utility poles.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks where the pedestrian sign indicates a crossing point to formalize the pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the crossing point to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers by preventing parking too close to the crossing.

result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides of a two-lane roadway with mixed residential and commercial land use. However, the environment lacks marked pedestrian crossings and physical traffic calming measures, with some sidewalk space obstructed by parked motorcycles.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Motorcycles are parked on the sidewalk area, narrowing the effective walking path for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of Marked Crossings
hazards.description: No marked pedestrian crossings are visible in this mixed-use block, requiring pedestrians to cross unmarked lanes.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks at intersections or appropriate mid-block locations to define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions at potential crossing points to shorten crossing distance and improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is dominated by a wide, unmarked driveway for an auto repair shop that interrupts the sidewalk continuity. There is a lack of clear separation between walking areas and vehicle maneuvering zones, creating significant conflict points.

hazards.name: Wide Driveway Conflict Zone
hazards.description: A very wide curb cut for the auto shop forces pedestrians to cross a large area where vehicles frequently maneuver without clear markings.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground, across the front of the T&M Auto Repair building.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Discontinuity
hazards.description: The paved sidewalk ends and transitions into a flush asphalt surface used for parking and vehicle access, reducing pedestrian predictability.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked in the lot adjacent to the street may block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers on the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image, vehicles parked in front of the building.

interventions.title: Delineated Sidewalk Crossing
interventions.description: Use high-visibility paint or contrasting materials to continue the sidewalk path across the wide driveway to alert drivers to the presence of pedestrians.

interventions.title: Driveway Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the width of the curb cut to the minimum necessary for vehicle access, restoring more of the protected curb and sidewalk area.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Warning Signage
interventions.description: Install signs warning drivers of pedestrian activity, especially near the auto shop entrance/exit.
